title: Shortest Subarray With OR at Least K I
statement:
You get an array `nums` of non-negative integers and an integer `k`. Call a non-empty contiguous subarray of `nums` **special** when OR-ing all of its elements together (bitwise OR) gives a value of `k` or more.

Return the length of the shortest special subarray. If `nums` has no special subarray, return `-1`.
notes:
## Intuition

With at most 50 numbers there are only about 1,275 subarrays, so enumerating them is the intended solution. One bit fact makes the enumeration lean: OR-ing in another number can only turn bits on, never off, so the OR of a subarray never shrinks as it grows to the right. For a fixed start, the first end where the OR reaches `k` gives the shortest special subarray from that start, and extending further is pointless.

## Approach

1. Set `best` to `Infinity` to mean "nothing found yet".
2. For each start index `left`, reset `orValue` to `0`.
3. Move `right` from `left` to the end, folding `nums[right]` into `orValue`.
4. As soon as `orValue >= k`, record the length `right - left + 1` in `best` if it is smaller, and stop extending this start.
5. Return `-1` if `best` is still `Infinity`, otherwise `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 3]`, `k = 2`.

- `left = 0`: `orValue` becomes `1` (too small), then `1 | 2 = 3`, which reaches 2, so `best = 2`.
- `left = 1`: `orValue = 2` already reaches 2, so `best = 1`.
- `left = 2`: `orValue = 3` reaches 2 with length 1; `best` stays `1`.

The answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): each start scans at most the rest of the array.
- Space: O(1): only a few counters.

## Pitfalls

- When `k = 0`, every single element is special (even `0`), so the answer is `1`.
- Reset `orValue` for every new start; carrying it over mixes in elements outside the subarray.
- Compare the OR with `>=`, not `>`: reaching `k` exactly counts.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `best` | shortest special length found so far |
| `left` | start index of the subarray |
| `right` | end index of the subarray |
| `orValue` | bitwise OR of `nums[left..right]` |

narration.3: No special subarray has been found yet, so the best length starts at Infinity.
narration.5: Try every index as the start of the subarray.
narration.6: A new start begins with an empty OR.
narration.7: Grow the subarray one element to the right at a time.
narration.8: Fold the new element into the OR; bits can only turn on.
narration.10: Yes: keep this length if it is the shortest so far.
narration.11: Longer subarrays from this start can only be longer, so stop here.
narration.15: Return -1 if nothing was special, otherwise the shortest length.
